# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 68 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 68 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_068_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 68 develops the theology of proportionate testing: the strong receive more difficult trials, the weak fewer, so that each may be "perfected" (*teleōthōsin*) or at least "not overwhelmed." This is a coherent theodicy: suffering is divinely calibrated to each person's capacity.

The eschatological wage (*misthos*) is introduced: after the full period, God will repay each person. "Wage" (*misthos*) is a commercial/agricultural term — the laborer's due payment. Hermas uses it consistently for eschatological reward.

The twofold outcome in 68:4: (1) those who endure without being "broken in mind" (*tēi dianoia*) receive great glory and live; (2) those who are broken receive neither glory nor life. The mind (*dianoia*) is the locus of endurance or collapse.

EMET's "not broken in mind" and LOGOS's "mind is not broken" both render *mē suntriphē tēi dianoia*. SOPHIA uses "not broken in mind" — the passive indicates what happens to them under the weight of trial.

---

## Similitude 6, Part 6 — Testing, Endurance, and Reward

**68:1** "I should also like to know, lord," I said, "why the Lord does not keep away from his servants the troubles and adversities of this life, but rather delivers them to these things." "He is unable to keep them away," he said, "for they must pass through all these things. The Lord has appointed these afflictions for the testing of those whom he has destined for such a test."

**68:2** "But why, lord, are some tested with fewer torments and others with many?" "Because," he said, "not all are equally able to endure. For some are weak in faith and some are strong. The strong must bear the greater trials so that they may be perfected; but the weak receive fewer trials, that they may not be completely overwhelmed."

**68:3** "The Lord watches over all who are afflicted and will repay to each person his wage according to his deeds. And after the full time has passed, the Lord will repay to each one his wage." "And will there be no mercy for those who are afflicted, lord?" I asked. "There will be mercy," he said.

**68:4** "But those who are afflicted and endure their afflictions and are not overcome by them — those who are not broken in mind — shall receive very great glory from the Lord. And those who are in affliction but do not overcome — those who are broken — shall receive none of this glory, nor shall they live to God. The one who keeps the commandments and endures through the afflictions shall receive life and grow great in it."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
